To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a quasi-three-dimensional model has been developed for heat transfer inside vertical ground heat exchanger boreholes, accounting for thermal interaction between the U-tubes, and an explicit solution of a line source model has been derived for long time steps.

(1) an explicit solution to a finite line-source heat transfer model is derived to describe temperature response of vertical ground heat exchange systems; and (2) an analytical expression of thermal resistance inside the vertical borehole is obtained by considering thermal interference between two U-tube legs, which is a function of thermal conductivity and thermal diffusivity of the surrounding soil.
a new explicit solution of the finite line-source model is derived, and a new quasi-three-dimensional model for heat transfer inside boreholes is developed.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new model for the thermal performance analysis of ground heat exchange systems.
the modeling of heat transfer in ground heat exchanger, the development of a more realistic model for heat transfer in ground source heat pump system.
the development of a new model for heat transfer analysis of vertical ground heat exchange, which is more accurate and more suitable for engineering application.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the models presented are more accurate than those available in literature and can be easily incorporated in computer programs for thermal simulation of ground-source heat pump system.
these models are more accurate than the conventional models and can be used in the analysis of heat transfer in ground-source heat pump system.
these models would help to improve the design procedures recommended by the available literature.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the heat transfer in ground heat exchanners is more complex than previously thought.

the thermal performance of vertical ground heat exchange systems can be predicted with reasonable accuracy by using the quasi-three-dimensional model for borehole heat transfer, the finite line-source model for temperature response of borehole, and the analytical model of ground temperature.

a better understanding of the thermal behavior of vertical ground heat-exchangers is obtained by the use of a quasi-three-dimensional model for heat transfer in boreholes and an explicit finite line-source model for the heat transfer from the boreholes to the ground.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the heat transfer model of the ground heat exchanger is a key component of the thermal design of ground-source heat pump system.
the quasi-three-dimensional model can be used for the thermal resistance of the borehole.
the quasi-3D model is the most accurate one, and the explicit solution of the finite line-source model is more suitable to describe the temperature response of borehole for long time steps.
